note: New theory types beyond day-of-week conditional patterns. Requires pattern_engine extension (see seasonal_momentum_handoff.md). Universe: Baltic Main List from master.parquet, 2005-2026, long-only, EUR.

theories.hypothesis: January returns on Baltic Main List stocks exceed the average of other calendar months. Effect expected to be pronounced because the entire Baltic market is small-cap and retail-driven (the documented driver of the January effect). Literature notes the effect has partially shifted to start mid-December.

variants.name: shifted_december_start
variants.baseline: all other days of year, same-length rolling windows

theories.portfolio: equal-weight across all Main List tickers with valid data in the window
metrics: mean window return vs baseline mean (same-length)
hit_rate: fraction of years window return > median monthly return of that year
hit_rate vs complement baseline via Fisher's exact (log-gamma implementation)
theories.stability_check: five multi-year sub-periods 2005-2026, same windows as Patterns 1-2
theories.execution_note: If confirmed: bias planned purchases toward early-to-mid December; do NOT trade as in-and-out (spread paid twice).

theories.hypothesis: November-April returns exceed May-October returns. Documented across 37 countries with the effect strongest in European markets; Baltic markets untested.
instruments: OMX Tallinn index (from master.parquet if present, else index proxy)
metrics: per-year winter minus summer return difference
hit_rate: fraction of years winter > summer
mean difference with bootstrap confidence interval (n_years ~ 21, LOW POWER - report CI, do not over-claim)
theories.stability_check: directional consistency across sub-periods; formal five-window split underpowered at ~4 obs each, report descriptively only
theories.execution_note: If confirmed: use as buy-timing bias (concentrate planned purchases Sep-Oct, avoid initiating in late April); NOT a sell-and-rebuy strategy on Baltic spreads.

theories.hypothesis: Stocks ranked in the top tercile by trailing 12-month return excluding the most recent month outperform the equal-weight Main List universe. Serial correlation (momentum) is among the most robust documented anomalies; illiquid small-cap markets often exhibit stronger momentum.

signal.ranking: total return over months t-12 to t-1
signal.eligibility: Main List only; minimum 12 months of price history; exclude tickers with >20% zero-volume days in lookback

portfolio.selection: top tercile (universe ~30-40 names, deciles too thin)

costs.spread_model: per-trade cost = estimated half-spread per ticker (median daily (ask-bid)/mid if available, else proxy from high-low estimator); apply on every entry and exit
costs.report: gross AND net returns; turnover per variant

theories.benchmark: equal-weight all eligible Main List names, same rebalance dates
metrics: annualized net excess return vs benchmark
hit_rate: fraction of rebalance periods top tercile > benchmark, Fisher's exact vs 50%

secondary_variant.rule: hold a name only if its own trailing 12-1 month return > 0; otherwise cash (long-only compatible trend filter)
secondary_variant.purpose: tests whether a time-series filter reduces drawdowns enough to justify added turnover cost

theories.execution_note: Quarterly rebalance is the realistic LHV retail variant; monthly likely eroded by spread. Judge tradability on NET numbers only.
